memory_maintenance.scope: ELF archive migration and memory measurements only; original UI observation above was not repeated.
memory_maintenance.method: Ten 1 Hz samples per phase; discard first, median of nine. Sync and POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED on the three archive ELFs only; no global drop_caches.
memory_maintenance.preserved: Current executable, font, logs, lock, initial pixels/pan and recovery tool remain at original paths; rollback ELF is persistent with the original path retained as a symlink.
memory_maintenance.verification_limit: No application restart, rollback launch, UI screenshot or display regression in this maintenance; font and recovery materials still reside in tmpfs.

memory_soak.verdict: Not fully stabilized in this run: Controls RSS continued to rise in steps and did not decline during the final two-minute idle. This does not by itself establish a memory leak.
memory_soak.method: Native Slint MCP drives the existing display process; external 1 Hz /proc sampler. No restart, screenshots, allocation probes, trim or manual cache clearing.

memory_growth_attribution.method: Read-only ARM glibc/TLS/VRc snapshots with all three threads briefly stopped; two independent mallinfo fixtures matched. Native Slint MCP controlled static-query and page-cycle groups; no screenshot/event recording.
memory_growth_attribution.verdict: Dynamic MCP element enumeration retains weak references to destroyed component allocations until handle eviction; minimal page cycles and static queries did not accumulate in these controlled groups. Allocator-free resident pages are a separate measured stock.
memory_growth_attribution.limitations: No allocator/MCP snapshot before the original 30-minute soak, so current chunk-byte stocks cannot be treated as the historical 1124 KiB heap RSS delta. Fixed-workload plateau is not a universal byte cap or proof that all showcase workloads are leak-free.
memory_growth_attribution.cleanup: 65 diagnostic files plus manifest archived and SHA256 verified, then removed from device; no diagnostic processes remain. Original display, font, rollback and recovery hashes unchanged.
